title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 4th District
area: Northern Kentucky, across the Ohio River from Cincinnati, including Covington, Florence and Ashland.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Thomas Massie (R) lost the May 19, 2026 Republican primary to Ed Gallrein.

candidates.name: Melissa Strange
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 72.4% of the vote, defeating Jesse Brewer.

summary.text: Melissa Strange is the Democratic nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. She campaigns on restoring trust in government, affordable cost of living, and protecting individual medical decision-making, including abortion access, from government interference.

priorities.text: "RESTORE FAITH AND TRUST IN GOVERNMENT ... Elected officials must conduct themselves with honesty, integrity, and transparency, demonstrating a clear commitment to public service, NOT to personal enrichment."

"AFFORDABLE AND ACCESSIBLE QUALITY OF LIFE ... All citizens should be able to afford basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, and education, and everyone deserves to be paid a fair, livable wage."

positions.summary: Campaign issues page lists getting government out of reproductive healthcare; her Ballotpedia survey says laws protecting access to such care must exist at the federal level.
positions.quote: Get the government out of your reproductive healthcare

positions.summary: Campaign issues page lists protecting and expanding Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security.
positions.quote: Protect and expand Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she wants to end tariffs she describes as inflationary.

statements.quote: everyone deserves to be paid a fair, livable wage.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026)

candidates.name: Ed Gallrein
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Thomas Massie in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary.

summary.text: Ed Gallrein is the Republican nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District, a farmer, business owner and U.S. Navy veteran. He campaigns on cutting taxes, reducing federal spending, border security, and gun rights.

background.text: Received a bachelor's degree and a master's degree from Murray State University.
Worked as a farmer and business owner; served in the U.S. Navy from 1984 to 2014.

priorities.text: Campaign website priorities: "Unleash Our Economy," "Secure the Border & Protect our Nation," "Defend Our Gun Rights," "Protect the Unborn," and "End the Woke Agenda."

statements.quote: Gallrein will team up with President Trump and the Republican Party to finish the wall, fully fund Border Patrol & ICE, secure the border once and for all
statements.context: Under "Secure the Border & Protect our Nation" on his campaign website

statements.quote: Gallrein will protect our right to keep and bear arms without compromise and back the blue.
statements.context: Under "Defend Our Gun Rights" on his campaign website
Under "Protect the Unborn" on his campaign website

summary.text: Jeremy Todd is the Libertarian Party nominee for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. He campaigns on reducing federal debt and money printing, ending U.S. overseas military commitments, and opposing government surveillance.

priorities.text: "As a Christian and a Libertarian, he believes in individual liberty, personal responsibility, limited government, and protecting the freedoms guaranteed to every American."
"If elected, I will focus on restoring financial sanity and easing this pressure, so that we can keep the American dream alive right here in our neighborhood."
"I will advocate to close our overseas bases, bring our brave troops back home to their loved ones, and focus our resources on defending our own homeland."
"That means stopping the spread of FLOCK cameras on our local streets, and banning any future implementation of Central Bank Digital Currencies and social credit systems."

positions.summary: Campaign website says he supports the SAVE Act, which he describes as requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
positions.quote: I support the SAVE Act because I believe American elections should be decided only by American citizens.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and supports returning abortion policy to the states, with no federal funding for abortion services.
positions.quote: That’s why I support returning the question of abortion policy to the states and to the democratic process closest to the people.

positions.summary: Campaign website says gun regulations burden responsible owners and that "gun safety" policies have failed.
positions.quote: So-called “gun-free zones” have too often become targets for those who seek to do harm, while endless regulations continue to burden responsible gun owners rather than criminals.

statements.quote: Our goal should be a dramatic reduction in taxation across the board, moving toward a system where people keep as much of what they earn as possible
statements.context: Campaign website, "Taxes and the Fed" issue page

statements.quote: I do not support open borders, because a functioning nation requires sovereignty, structure, and the ability to know who is entering and residing within its territory.

summary.text: Peter Harmon Williams is an independent write-in candidate for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District. No campaign website, public statements, or biographical profile were found for this candidate.

sources.title: Kentucky's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
sources.publisher: Ballotpedia (Candidate Connection survey for Strange, Todd; staff-compiled for Gallrein)

researchNotes: Open seat: Thomas Massie lost the Republican primary. Strange, Gallrein and Todd positions and statements come from their campaign websites and Strange's and Todd's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection surveys; Gallrein has not completed the Ballotpedia survey and his site has no issue pages beyond five priority headings. Todd's earlier Israel-aid entry was removed because his cited statement is about closing overseas bases generally, not Israel aid. No campaign website, questionnaire or news coverage was found for write-in candidate Peter Harmon Williams (Kentucky Secretary of State lists a write-in filing dated Aug. 21, 2026); no positions added.
